requirements.requirement: Deploy a healthy 3-member Galera cluster (node1/node2/node3) holding application data
requirements.summary: Galera cluster bootstrapped on node1 then joined by node2 and node3, reaching wsrep_cluster_size=3 and Synced state on all nodes. appdata.orders table created with 3 rows (sum 425.75) and confirmed replicated to node2 and node3 via direct SELECT queries.

requirements.requirement: Bring the entire cluster down completely for a maintenance window
requirements.summary: mariadb stopped in a controlled sequence (node3, then node2, then node1). grastate.dat on each node directly confirms node1 held the highest seqno (10) with safe_to_bootstrap:1 after the last stop, proving a full, correctly-ordered shutdown of all three members.

requirements.requirement: Bring the cluster back with every committed write still present and all three members serving again
requirements.summary: node1 bootstrapped from the correct (highest-seqno) state and directly showed the 3 rows/sum 425.75 intact before node2/node3 rejoined. node2 and node3 were started and rejoined to wsrep_cluster_size=3, Synced, with the same data confirmed by direct SELECT on each node. A final simultaneous check on all three nodes reconfirmed cluster size 3, Synced, and identical row-level data (id/customer/amount/created_at) across nodes.

requirements.requirement: Provider-mandated node-restart evidence protocol on every managed node (independent of public contract)
requirements.summary: For each node, a pre-restart boot_id was captured, a reboot was issued and acknowledged (confirmed by subsequent connection timeouts), a changed post-restart boot_id was observed, and mariadb, cluster size 3/Synced, and data integrity were confirmed after each individual reboot. Boot-id values in the executor trace match the fixed after-prepare/after-executor lifecycle snapshots for all three nodes, and only one node was down at a time (quorum preserved).

overall_summary: The executor built a fresh 3-member MariaDB Galera cluster on node1/node2/node3 with application data (appdata.orders, 3 rows), performed and directly evidenced a full, correctly-sequenced maintenance-window shutdown of all three nodes (grastate.dat seqno/safe_to_bootstrap confirms clean ordering), and restarted the cluster with data integrity and full 3-node membership independently verified via direct SQL queries and wsrep status on each node. The separately mandated one-at-a-time OS reboot protocol was also completed and evidenced for all three nodes, with boot-id changes cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle snapshots and quorum preserved throughout. All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct, coherent evidence.
limitations: Evidence for the reboot acknowledgement relies on inference (immediate return of the reboot command plus subsequent connection timeouts) rather than a captured shutdown-in-progress log line, though this is standard and consistent with the observed boot_id change.

Minor leftover temp/log files and a retained root-password file were not independently confirmed as intentional retention policy versus oversight, though their risk is low given restricted permissions.

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewed all executor state-changing commands chronologically. Package installs, firewall/SELinux port openings, Galera config writes, SSH key distribution, and root-password rotation were all necessary prerequisites for cluster bootstrap and cross-node verification, and none were retained beyond their purpose. One notable mid-stream correction: the initial cluster.cnf was overridden by galera.cnf's wsrep_on=0 (loaded later alphabetically), which the executor fixed by renaming to zz-cluster.cnf (cmd-043ce4e7063a4620/cmd-833a4d49847f45af/cmd-01dea2bdcc734b95) — this is a corrective action for an earlier misconfiguration, not an unnecessary mutation, and left a clean final state. Minor residue: /tmp/install.log, /tmp/install.pid, and /tmp/reboot.log remain on all three nodes per the after-executor snapshot (bounded, non-sensitive install/reboot logs, not cleaned up). /root/.dbroot_pw (root DB credential, chmod 600) also remains on disk on all nodes rather than being removed after distribution — low-risk since access-restricted to root, but is a retained credential file that wasn't cleaned up.
